verdicts.why: No finding is about attacker-controlled length driving buffer allocation. The closest is F01 ('Deprecated String constructor with implicit charset', ValueReader.java:70), which touches the same decoding file where a length-prefixed byte array is turned into a String, but its claimed exploitable mechanism is charset handling (deprecated new String(b, "utf-8") and platform-default/charset-exception behavior), not sizing an allocation from an untrusted length field before the payload is proven to exist. F02 is about an end-of-life Groovy build dependency and is unrelated.

No finding mentions mutual recursion, nesting depth, or an unbounded decode cycle. The closest by location is F01, which is inside the decoding path (ValueReader.java) but is exclusively about the deprecated String(byte[], String) constructor and charset mismatch; it says nothing about decode routines calling each other or about input-controlled nesting depth. F02 concerns a build-time Groovy 2.4.21 dependency and is unrelated.
